# 1 Enoch Chapter 83 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

This log records all verses in 1 Enoch Chapter 83 where the three translators (EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA) significantly diverged in their renderings, along with SOPHIA's resolution and reasoning.

---

## 83:3 — 'collapsed and was borne off' vs. 'caved in' vs. 'fell'

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "the-heaven-collapsed and-was-borne-off and-fell-to-the-earth" | Three-stage destruction: collapse, removal, fall |
| LOGOS | "the heaven collapsed and was borne off and fell to the earth" | Preserves the three stages |
| PNEUMA | "the sky caved in — it broke apart, came crashing down" | Vivid but reduces three stages to two |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS rendering with all three stages. The Ge'ez text describes a three-stage process: (1) the heaven collapsed/broke, (2) it was borne off/removed, (3) it fell to earth. These are distinct motions in the cosmological vision and should not be compressed.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS/EMET. Three stages preserved.

---

## 83:5 — 'a word fell into my mouth'

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "a-word-fell-into-my-mouth" | Literal; the prophetic word is experienced passively |
| LOGOS | "a word fell into my mouth" | Same |
| PNEUMA | "a cry burst out of me" | Dynamic; loses the passive reception of the word |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS 'a word fell into my mouth.' This is a distinctive prophetic idiom — the word comes from outside and is received by the prophet. PNEUMA's 'a cry burst out of me' makes the act internal rather than external reception, losing the prophetic dimension.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS/EMET. Prophetic reception preserved.

---

## 83:8 — 'since thou art a believer' / 'you are a believer'

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "since-thou-art-a-believer" | Literal Ge'ez term for 'faithful one' |
| LOGOS | "since you are a believer" | Same with modern pronoun |
| PNEUMA | "You are a man of faith" | Slightly amplified |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS 'since you are a believer.' The Ge'ez term (haymanot) means one who has faith/trust. PNEUMA's addition of 'a man of' is not in the source. The designation qualifies why Enoch's prayer will be effective.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---
